A liquidity shock or flash crash scenario could even push through the one-day lower bound. Correlation breaks, where assets that normally hedge each other move in the same direction, represent another tail risk not fully captured here. In short, the intervals should be treated as reasonable central-case bounds under normal market conditions, not as guarantees that extreme outcomes are impossible.
